EDITORIAL NOTES

Text and translation notes

  1. The first Adam in v.1 is read as the genealogical figure; adam in the creation clause is rendered as humankind. BDB120 includes men and women at5:1 and collective naming at5:2. English collective them interprets a singular Hebrew object. The collective name Humankind in v.2 shares its Hebrew spelling and sound with Adam; it is not restricted to males.
  2. BDB8435 treats toledot as a genealogical account of a person and descendants. Record does not establish an extant autograph by Adam or identify an ancient author. Likeness and image are translated without imposing separate doctrinal categories. Son in v.3 supplies an object from context; Seth is not identified as Adam’s first child.
  3. Verses3–5 retain the pinned WLC numbers130,800 after Seth,and930 total,and he died. Their arithmetic agrees; historical dating and biological lifespan were not independently verified. The number or birth dates of other children and completeness of the genealogy remain unspecified. Other ancient version numbers were not collated.
  4. Verses6–8 retain105 years before Seth fathered Enosh,807 afterward,and912 total.105+807=912 checks textual arithmetic,not historical lifespan. Verses9–10 retain Enosh’s90 years and815 after fathering Kenan,without adding a death notice absent from this batch. Kenan is a translation spelling of the Hebrew name and is not identified with Cain.
  5. Verses11–15 retain Enosh’s905 total years,Kenan’s70 years before Mahalalel and840 afterward,910 total,and Mahalalel’s65 years before Jared.90+815=905 and70+840=910 check textual arithmetic,not historical lifespans. First-born status,genealogical completeness and death notices absent from these verses are not added. Name spellings are editorial transliterations,not etymological claims.
